title: Burst headroom telemetry gap and graceful-degradation strategy for reserved pools
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: A production escalation from multiple customers (one enterprise with a reserved pool) revealed that under sustained non-bursty tail traffic the reserved-pool headroom calculation drifted negative and the autoscaler rate limiter prevented compensating scale-ups, exhausting burst capacity. Additionally, a telemetry ingestion gap caused the controller to under-report available headroom for 11 minutes, delaying mitigations.
description: What happened: During a weekday afternoon surge where several customers drove long tail requests to the Dedicated fleet, the headroom estimator returned stale metrics due to a drop in the metrics ingestion pipeline (metrics aggregator GC pause + brief SQS throttling). The autoscaler uses a rate-limited scale action queue; during the gap the controller attempted multiple compensatory scale actions but were rate-limited and queued. When metrics resumed, the estimator reconciled but the effective burst-accounting had already depleted the pool. Impact: one enterprise customer saw 7 minutes of higher latency with token throttling errors and 2 customers received degraded QoS. Engineering pager fired and customer SREs escalated to support.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 14:03 - latency increases observed by customer dashboards; 14:06 - internal alerts (consumer tail latency); 14:08 - metrics aggregator GC spike; 14:19 - SQS throttling spikes; 14:20 - controller metrics gap ends; 14:26 - reserved pool exhausted; 14:30 - fallback policies triggered and traffic shifted to lower-tier model variants. Findings: 1) telemetry aggregator can pause under high cardinality GC conditions for ~10 minutes. 2) autoscaler rate-limiter has a coarse per-pool token refill that doesn't account for burstbackoff detection. 3) headroom accounting and burst budget reconciler apply corrections only at 5-minute windows, causing slow recovery. Evidence: graphs in linked Confluence doc, controller logs (correlation IDs attached), and a reproduced load test that shows headroom desync when ingestion dropped.
root_cause: A combination of (A) metrics ingestion gap (GC + intermittent SQS throttling) causing stale headroom inputs, and (B) autoscaler rate-limiter policy that prevented timely compensating scale-ups. Secondary: burst-accounting reconciliation interval was too coarse for short recoveries.
mitigation_actions_taken: Deployed emergency hotfix to bypass rate-limiter for critical compensating scale requests (hotfix #PR-1642)
Enabled temporary aggressive fallback routing to compatible hosted models for affected customers
Applied a short-term patch to reduce GC pressure by increasing aggregator heap and adjusting retention filters
customer_communications: 2026-02-10 15:00 - Initial acknowledgement sent to affected customers with incident summary and ETA for next update
2026-02-10 17:45 - Customer-facing follow-up: hotfix deployed, mitigation steps and credit offer; Incident RCA committed to Confluence; dedicated follow-up meeting scheduled with enterprise SREs
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: reduce autoscaler rate-limiter strictness for compensating scale actions to favor availability over transient cost spikes. Tradeoff: small, controlled cost increase during edge surges versus preventing customer-facing throttles.
Decision: shorten burst-accounting reconciliation from 5 minutes to 30s for critical reserved pools. Tradeoff: heavier accounting churn and slightly noisier metrics but faster recovery.
Decision: maintain telemetry aggregator heap increase as short-term fix while working on long-term ingestion resiliency. Tradeoff: resource footprint increase on metrics cluster.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix validated with synthetic load test reproducing prior failure mode and showing no headroom desync in 15/15 runs
New e2e test added to CI that simulates an ingestion gap and verifies graceful degradation/path to recovery
Dashboarding: alert for metrics-staleness triggers at 30s and automatically escalates; headroom-staleness runbook created and verified with runbook drill
next_steps: Implement resilient metrics ingestion (idempotent buffering + backoff-aware consumer) - tracked in ENG-904210
Refactor autoscaler token refill to use adaptive refill rates informed by recent scale failures - tracked in ENG-933001
Add canary rollout of reduced rate-limiter to 10% of pools and monitor for cost/regression over 1 week
Formalize customer SLO playbooks for reserved-pool degradations and credits approval flow

notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: please validate PR-1642 safety checks and ensure no edge path allows uncontrolled scale-flapping. Pay special attention to the canary plan and the cost guardrails. Confirm e2e test coverage covers both short ingestion gaps (30s-2m) and longer gaps (5-15m).
